deliverables: DeFi Kernel registry website and submission process with compatibility requirements, metadata requirements, documentation, onboarding, monthly progress reports, and final impact report

Cardano-native DeFi Kernel-compatible Spot Leverage Order Book with protocol design, testnet deployment, security review or audit, mainnet release, published script hashes and schemas, adoption reporting, and integration documentation

Cardano-native American Options Market-Making protocol with protocol design, testnet deployment, security review or audit, mainnet release, published script hashes and schemas, adoption reporting, and integration documentation

Composable DeFi Transaction Builder SDK with registry schema reader, metadata parser, discovery helpers, transaction-construction helpers, adapters, public documentation, examples, tests, integration support, and final SDK report
request.recipient: Dano Finance, with Minswap Labs serving as budget administrator
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Dano Finance's DeFi Kernel registry, Spot Leverage Order Book, American Options Market-Making Pools, and Composable DeFi Transaction Builder SDK.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,333,000 ADA total, consisting of 3,300,000 ADA for delivery and a 33,000 ADA 1% administration fee for Minswap Labs.

Dano Finance will improve the public defikernel.org platform and registry so Cardano builders can submit compatible smart contracts and publish metadata needed by wallets, bots, indexers, and protocols.
The DeFi Kernel is intended to be an open, fee-free, royalty-free compatibility standard that does not require listing fees, licensing fees, revenue share, or smart-contract open-sourcing.
Dano Finance currently has approximately USD 18M in TVL and more than 10,000 on-chain transactions.
The Spot Leverage Order Book will support leveraged spot trading intents involving collateral, borrowing, debt accounting, position management, repayment, liquidation conditions, and settlement.
The American Options Market-Making protocol will use an extended concentrated-pool model to let liquidity providers supply capital and users buy or exercise pool-priced American options.
The SDK will help wallets, bots, indexers, market makers, and dApps discover financial intent, read registry metadata, construct transactions, and compose with DeFi Kernel-compatible contracts.
Mainnet launches for the smart contract workstreams are conditioned on security review or audit, issue resolution, and unresolved critical security issues blocking affected mainnet milestones.

The proposal targets at least USD 1,000,000 in rolling 30-day trading volume for the Spot Leverage Order Book and USD 1,000,000 in rolling 30-day option notional volume for the American Options protocol within 90 days of mainnet launch, measured using public on-chain data.

Dano Finance states it will return 5% of protocol fees from the Treasury-funded Spot Leverage Order Book and American Options contracts for 12 months after mainnet launch, calculated after direct transaction costs, refunds, or protocol-level settlement costs and reported publicly.

summary: The document requests 3,333,000 ADA for Dano Finance to deliver a DeFi Kernel registry, two DeFi protocols, and an SDK, administered by Minswap Labs, with milestone structure, security review conditions, adoption KPIs, public reporting, and a limited 5% protocol-fee return commitment.
